content.text: /ext:medcp Did prescription rates of systemic immunosuppressants decline in 2020 compared with 2019?
I'll check the clinical database to answer this. Let me first see what tables are available.

This is an OMOP CDM database. Systemic immunosuppressants map to an ATC class in the OMOP vocabulary. I'll identify the drug concepts via ATC L04 (Immunosuppressants) using `concept_ancestor`, then count distinct drug exposures per year (2019 vs 2020) in `drug_exposure`.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT concept_id, concept_name, concept_code, vocabulary_id, concept_class_id
FROM omop.concept
WHERE vocabulary_id = 'ATC' AND concept_code = 'L04'

content.text: Found the ATC class node (concept_id 21603890, "IMMUNOSUPPRESSANTS", L04). Now I'll count drug exposures for descendant drug concepts by year.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS yr,
       COUNT(*) AS n_exposures,
       COUNT(DISTINCT de.person_id) AS n_patients
FROM omop.drug_exposure de
JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON de.drug_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 21603890
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM de.drug_exposure_start_date) IN (2019, 2020)
GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM de.drug_exposure_start_date)
ORDER BY yr

content.text: This is SQL Server. I'll use `YEAR()` instead of `EXTRACT`.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT YEAR(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS yr,
       COUNT(*) AS n_exposures,
       COUNT(DISTINCT de.person_id) AS n_patients
FROM omop.drug_exposure de
JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON de.drug_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 21603890
  AND YEAR(de.drug_exposure_start_date) IN (2019, 2020)
GROUP BY YEAR(de.drug_exposure_start_date)
ORDER BY yr

content.text:
No — prescription rates of systemic immunosuppressants (ATC L04) **rose** in 2020 versus 2019 in this database.

| Year | Exposures | Distinct patients |
|------|-----------|-------------------|
| 2019 | 243,677 | 12,602 |
| 2020 | 272,184 | 13,627 |

2020 shows ~11.7% more exposure records and ~8.1% more patients receiving these drugs. So there was no decline; the count increased.

Caveats: this is a raw count within one OMOP database, not a population-adjusted rate (no denominator for enrolled/active patients per year), and it counts all L04 drug_exposure records. If you want a true rate, I can normalize by the number of persons with an active observation period each year, or break it down by specific agent.
